error.signature: AI tells someone that they need to download an app, register their phone number, or subscribe to a service to receive Brazil's official natural-disaster warnings

verdict.summary: Brazil's Defesa Civil Alerta reached full nationwide Cell Broadcast coverage on 1 October 2025: extreme/severe risk warnings are pushed automatically to every compatible phone on a 4G or 5G network inside the risk area, with no app, account, or registration involved. The real gaps are a 4G/5G-only requirement (2G/3G-only devices/networks receive nothing) and, after a June 2026 breach sent 10 false alerts to millions of phones, that receiving an alert through the official channel is not on its own proof the content is genuine.

dead_ends.action: Search for and install a 'Defesa Civil' app, or sign up online, believing that's required to receive extreme-risk alerts
dead_ends.why_fails: ANATEL's public guidance confirms no registration, app download, or subscription is required: Defesa Civil Alerta operates automatically via Cell Broadcast on any phone connected to a 4G or 5G network inside the alerted area, with national coverage complete since 1 October 2025.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Most other notification systems (weather apps, news alerts) do require an install or subscription, so people assume a government disaster-alert system works the same way.

dead_ends.action: Assume you'll receive Defesa Civil Alerta warnings on any phone or network, since Brazil now advertises 'nationwide' coverage
dead_ends.why_fails: Cell Broadcast in Brazil is delivered only over 4G and 5G networks. A phone that is 2G/3G-only, in an area with only 2G/3G coverage, or a basic non-smartphone handset will not receive the alert at all, even though the programme itself reached every municipality by October 2025.
dead_ends.common_misconception: 'Nationwide coverage' as announced by MIDR/ANATEL describes which municipalities the programme can reach, not a guarantee that every device or connection in them will detect an alert.

dead_ends.action: Treat every message that arrives through the Defesa Civil Alerta Cell Broadcast channel as automatically authentic and act on its content immediately, with no cross-check, purely because it came through the official government channel
dead_ends.why_fails: On the night of 19-20 June 2026 the system was compromised: Brazil's National Secretary of Civil Protection confirmed 10 false alerts (9 via Cell Broadcast, 1 via SMS) were pushed to millions of phones before access was deactivated and the Federal Police opened an investigation. Arriving through the real channel is not on its own proof of authenticity; unusual or nonsensical content is worth cross-checking against official Defesa Civil / state civil-defense social channels.
dead_ends.condition: Message content is unusual, nonsensical, or otherwise inconsistent with a real hazard warning

workarounds.action: For a 4G/5G smartphone inside an alerted risk area, do nothing extra - the alert arrives automatically
workarounds.how: Keep an active SIM/eSIM connected to a 4G or 5G network; no app install or registration step exists for the federal alert.

workarounds.action: If on a 2G/3G-only device or network, or wanting a redundant channel, follow the relevant state/municipal Defesa Civil's own app or official social media account instead of assuming Cell Broadcast alone covers you
workarounds.how: State civil-defense agencies (e.g. Parana's and Rio Grande do Sul's Defesa Civil) publish their own apps and social channels as a backup to the federal Cell Broadcast system.
workarounds.tradeoff: Coverage and update frequency vary by state.

workarounds.action: Cross-check any alert with unusual or nonsensical wording against official Defesa Civil / state civil-defense social media or gov.br before treating it as either a real emergency or dismissing it outright
workarounds.how: During the June 2026 false-alarm incident, official channels confirmed the breach and correction within hours; checking those channels distinguishes a compromised broadcast from a genuine hazard warning.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers which number to dial to request help (citizen-to-government); this one covers Brazil's inbound government-to-citizen mass warning system, an unrelated one-way channel.
